title: Notebooks
tagline: Notebooks connected to the local database, in JupyterLab, Marimo or your Positron - one folder per persona.
role: Installs Exasol's notebook connector (the package AI Lab is built on), pyexasol, the Langfuse and OpenAI clients, the kit's notebook helpers and a Jupyter kernel named 'Exasol (Starter Kit)' in an environment of their own, then asks which notebook tools, all three ticked: JupyterLab (yours is used; with none, the kit's is installed because it was ticked), Marimo (installed into the kit's notebook environment) and Positron (yours, only ever configured: the notebooks folder names the kit's Python as its interpreter; the kit never installs Positron).
credentials: The connection lives in the connector's encrypted configuration store (~/.exasol-starter-kit/notebook/connection.scs). Its master password and the JupyterLab token are kit credentials in ~/.exasol-starter-kit/credentials, readable by you only. The kernel's spec names only those two file paths, and the helpers read them, so no kernel spec, notebook or output ever holds a secret. The notebooks connect as the kit's admin user, because building tables and UDFs needs it.
installed_by: exakit marketplace notebook (EXAKIT_MARKETPLACE_ADDONS=notebook for a script).
platforms: macOS on Apple silicon, Linux x86_64 (including WSL) and Windows x86_64. The connector supports Python 3.11 and 3.12; the kit's managed interpreter is 3.12. Linux on Arm is not offered: one of the connector's dependencies publishes no Linux Arm build.

quickstart.note: About 1 GB: the connector brings PyTorch for its transformer features (the CPU-only build on Linux). Then one checklist: JupyterLab, Marimo, Positron - all ticked; untick any you do not want.

JupyterLab in the background, opened in your browser, logged in, on ~/.exasol-starter-kit/notebooks. The kit's notebooks are in starter-kit-notebooks/, one folder per persona (general, data-scientist, ml-engineer), with a README naming the end-to-end path.
The same notebooks as Marimo notebooks, from notebooks/marimo/<persona>/.
Your Positron, opened on the notebooks folder with the kit's Python as the interpreter.

commands.summary: Start JupyterLab in the background, connected, and open it; --marimo does the same for Marimo (installing it when you say yes), --positron opens your Positron on the notebooks with the kit's Python; --stop stops JupyterLab and Marimo (--stop --marimo only Marimo); --check proves the connection; --setup settles a tool without starting it.

notes: The notebook tools are one checklist at the install, all three ticked. A JupyterLab already on your machine is used as it is; the kit only adds its kernel, 'Exasol (Starter Kit)', which VS Code and other Jupyter front ends offer too. Marimo goes into the kit's notebook environment. Positron is never installed: when it is there, the notebooks folder is set to the kit's Python (.vscode/settings.json, your other settings kept); when it is not, the folder is ready for it (https://positron.posit.co/download.html). For a script: EXAKIT_NOTEBOOK_FRONTENDS=jupyterlab,marimo,positron (or none); EXAKIT_NOTEBOOK_JUPYTER=skip or EXAKIT_NOTEBOOK_MARIMO=skip leaves one out. Untick one now, add it later with exakit notebook --setup, --marimo or --positron.
In Jupyter choose the kernel 'Exasol (Starter Kit)' for a notebook of your own. In Marimo, Positron or a plain script the kit's notebook Python finds the connection by itself.

In a notebook: import exakit_nb; conn = exakit_nb.connect() opens the database, exakit_nb.sql(conn, '...') runs a query into a DataFrame and remembers it, and exakit_nb.show_sql() prints the last statement.

Model-call tracing is opt-in: with LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY and LANGFUSE_HOST set before exakit notebook, exakit_nb.trace(...) records the calls in your own Langfuse project. Without them it says tracing is off and does nothing else.

Exasol's AI Lab notebooks that use only the database run here. Those that upload to BucketFS, install the Transformers or Text AI extensions or deploy a container through BucketFS do not: a local Exasol Personal database has no BucketFS upload service. Use exakit udf-file and exakit udf-use instead.
A notebook you edited is never overwritten: an update copies only notebooks you do not have yet.
An AI Lab or a JupyterLab of your own on the same machine is left alone.

explore.ipynb runs on any dataset with a descriptor: set DATASET in its first code cell to pharma_trials, banking_complaints, or the path of your own descriptor.json, and every query is built from the descriptor's roles and printed before its result. A small scikit-learn model trains on this computer. Its text step sends a few rows to your own model endpoint only when EXAKIT_NB_MODEL (the model name) is set before exakit notebook, with the endpoint and key in OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY; with the LANGFUSE_* variables set too, those calls are one trace tagged with the dataset, the descriptor's digest, the database session and the SQL.

train.ipynb trains a text classifier inside the database with a Python UDF (the database's own Python and scikit-learn) and logs the run with exasol-mlflow from the notebook: parameters, metrics, the training SQL, the model file and the session, statement and deployment it came from. The run goes to MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI when set before exakit notebook, else to a local MLflow store in the mlflow folder beside the notebook. The UDF holds no MLflow credentials and needs no network.

The kit's notebooks, one folder per persona, in the order of the end-to-end path: general/start_here, data-scientist/explore, data-scientist/text_classification (classify the FDA recalls' or the banking complaints' text), ml-engineer/bank_marketing_mlflow (four classifiers on the bank marketing clients, every run logged to MLflow) and ml-engineer/train. What goes where is notebook/catalog.json in the kit: adding a notebook is one entry there and its file, no code.

troubleshooting.symptom: JupyterLab is not installed, so the notebooks have nothing to open in
This notebook is not running on the kit's kernel
exakit notebook says the add-on is not installed
JupyterLab does not start because another Jupyter answers on the port
JupyterLab did not answer in time
explore.ipynb says the descriptor does not match the database
